2608.18759.title: Beyond Predictive Fairness: Quantifying Attribution Consistency Across Demographic Groups in Diabetic Retinopathy Screening
2608.18759.paper_summary: Fairness in medical imaging is commonly evaluated through subgroup performance metrics, yet it remains unclear whether models rely on consistent visual evidence across demographic groups. This work introduces the Explanation Consistency Score (ECS), a fairness-aware metric based on Jensen-Shannon divergence that quantifies the similarity of attribution maps across subgroups. Using diabetic retinopathy screening as a case study, ECS is evaluated globally and within disease severity. Experiments reveal that while predictive performance differs across ethnic groups, explanation consistency remains relatively high and shows no significant association with performance disparities. These findings suggest that predictive fairness and explanation consistency capture complementary dimensions of model behavior, motivating fairness evaluations that extend beyond predictive performance.
2608.18759.paper_summary_zh: 醫學影像中的公平性通常通過子群體表現指標來評估，但目前尚不清楚模型是否依賴於不同人口群體之間一致的視覺證據。這項工作引入了解釋一致性分數（ECS），這是一種基於詹森-香農散度的公平性意識指標，用於量化子群體之間的歸因圖相似性。以糖尿病視網膜病變篩查為案例，ECS在全球和疾病嚴重程度內進行評估。實驗顯示，儘管預測性能在不同族裔群體之間存在差異，但解釋一致性仍然相對較高，並且與性能差異之間沒有顯著關聯。這些發現表明，預測公平性和解釋一致性捕捉了模型行為的互補維度，促使公平性評估超越預測性能的範疇。
2608.18759.author: Kerol Djoumessi et.al.
